newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan against U.N. police capturing war criminals.
newsitem.headline: Annan against U.N. police capturing war criminals.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the new U.N. secretary-general elect, on Wednesday spoke against a U.N.-organised police force hunting down war criminals in the former Yugoslavia, a task NATO-led troops had refused.
"I am not sure that the UNIPTF. which has a limited mandate, is the force," he said, referring to the U.N. International Police Task Force currently in Bosnia.

This was particularly true when the NATO-led Implementation Force "with a much superior force" had hesitated in carrying out such an operation, he said at his first news conference since being appointed to the top U.N. job.
Annan, the current head of peacekeeping, was in charge of U.N. peacekeepers in Bosnia and presided during the handover between soldiers under a U.N. flag and the IFOR operation last year.
"It is essential that criminals be brought to justice because justice and peace is indivisible," he said.

"We need to press the governments of the region to cooperate and here I am talking about Serbia, Croatia and the government of Bosnia, which perhaps has cooperated a bit more than the others," he added.
In Brussels on Wednesday, NATO defence ministers proposed a new international police force to hunt down accused war crimes fugitives. They said the force that would have to be protected by troops.

But U.S. and NATO officials also said that the ministers were divided on how a police force might be set up and who would provide members to arrest fugitives and turn them over for prosecution by a U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague.
Annan also said the United Nations had learned from its mistakes in fielding peacekeepers, including the formner U.N. Protection Force (UNPROFOR) in the Balkans.

"We have learned that a clear mandate is necessary. We have learned that the resources should be commensorate to the tasks. We have learned that we should go into the theatre with a force and a force structure that is capable of carrying out its mandate and defending itself," he said.
"We have learned contrary to past hesitations that intelligence is necessary and that we need to have solid political analysis," he added.

"It is also important that we explain to the public and to the media our mandate and why we are on the ground, what we are there to do and what we are not there to do. And I think we did not do too well in Bosnia."

In comparison, Annan said "IFOR has defined its mandate narrowly and clearly and has constantly repeated it and told the public what they will do and not do" while "UNPROFOR was seens as everything to everybody."
